title: Where must the rest of the heat go?
hook: A heat engine runs between a hot and a cold reservoir.

knows: the quantities named in the question
doesNotKnow: For an ideal reversible engine the maximum efficiency is 1 − T_cold / T_hot. At 600 K and 300 K, at most half the input heat becomes work; the rest is rejected to the cold reservoir.

misconception: The alternative answers in the prediction appear plausible without the stated physical model.
objective: For an ideal reversible engine the maximum efficiency is 1 − T_cold / T_hot. At 600 K and 300 K, at most half the input heat becomes work; the rest is rejected to the cold reservoir.

claims.text: For an ideal reversible engine the maximum efficiency is 1 − T_cold / T_hot. At 600 K and 300 K, at most half the input heat becomes work; the rest is rejected to the cold reservoir. Temperatures must be absolute. Real engines have additional losses and perform below this ideal bound.

recall.question: An ideal reversible engine runs between 800 K and 600 K. What is its maximum efficiency?
